assigned.title: The fail-closed deployment path is asserted by nobody, because CI runs two of three configurations
assigned.acceptance:
FOUND BY MEASUREMENT IN ROUND 108: the development and production suites were both run to completion and their SKIP LISTS intersected. Five e2e titles are skipped in BOTH, so no configuration this repository executes ever runs them. Two are media-rig rows that correctly need the commander's hardware. THE OTHER THREE ASSERT A FAIL-CLOSED SECURITY BEHAVIOUR: 'a deployment with no identity system - fails closed with 503 and names the operator's remedy', '- publishes nothing only a resolver could know' (playback-session.api.spec.ts), and 'a deployment with no identity system refuses honestly rather than showing an empty list' (watchlist.spec.ts).

They need PRODUCTION MODE WITH NO DATABASE -- the third configuration. ci.yml runs exactly two: development, and production with PostgreSQL. The tests are not broken: run locally in that third configuration the full chromium+api suite gives 62 passed / 56 skipped / 0 failed.

REQUIRED: the third configuration runs in CI and fails the build when it fails.
REQUIRED: the cost is stated rather than absorbed. A third suite run adds to every push; the acceptance is that the fail-closed path is covered, not that it is covered in the most expensive available way. If a narrower invocation -- the three titles, or the two specs -- buys the same coverage for less, take it and say why.
REQUIRED: the three titles actually EXECUTE in the new configuration. Evidence is the run naming them as passed, not a count that went up.
REQUIRED: the two media-rig titles stay skipped and stay reasoned. They are RIG rows in PW-0601's matrix and must not be made to look covered.
REQUIRED: no existing configuration loses coverage, and no skip loses its reason.

OUT OF SCOPE: changing what the three tests assert, and relaxing any of them to make a cheaper configuration reach them.
assigned.notes:
CREATED IN ROUND 108. DEPENDS ON PL-0714 because that task owns .github/workflows/ci.yml and is in REVIEW; editing the file from here while it is an active surface would be the overlapping-surface collision the operating model forbids. Sequenced, not blocked.

THE PATTERN THIS IS THE FOURTH INSTANCE OF, recorded so the next one is found by a check rather than by accident: scripts/test-validate-repo.mjs ran nowhere until PL-AI-0002; scripts/test-desktop-target.mjs and the 30-case Windows lifecycle suite ran nowhere until PL-0714; apps/web/src/components/player/tracks.ts was imported by nothing until PW-0306 wired it. Each time the thing existed, passed, and no gate asked it. A standing mechanical check for 'skipped in every configuration we run' would have found all four, and proposing one is a reasonable thing for this task's implementation to consider -- the measurement that found this was two suite runs and a set intersection.

CONFLICT-CHECKED IN BOTH FIELDS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AT FILING: .github/workflows/ci.yml is held by PL-0714 (REVIEW) and by PL-0001, PL-0704, PL-AI-0002 and PW-0312, all DONE. The dependency on PL-0714 is what keeps the two from being active together. The reviewDependencies are read-only here: e2e/tests/watchlist.spec.ts belongs to PL-0715 (REVIEW) and is NOT written by this task.

e2e.evidence:
THE THIRD CONFIGURATION RUNS, THE THREE TITLES EXECUTE IN IT, AND THE GUARD THAT SAYS SO WAS PROVEN TO REFUSE.

MEASURED FIRST, DECIDED SECOND. All three configurations were run to completion locally with a JSON reporter and their executed sets compared:

  development              ran 122  skipped 29   274.8s
  production + PostgreSQL  ran 100  skipped 51    99.0s
  production, NO database  ran  71  skipped 80    75.4s

Tests the third configuration runs that NEITHER other one does -- computed as C minus (A union B), not asserted -- are EXACTLY three:
  [api]      playback-session.api.spec.ts > a deployment with no identity system > fails closed with 503 and names the operator's remedy
  [api]      playback-session.api.spec.ts > a deployment with no identity system > publishes nothing only a resolver could know
  [chromium] watchlist.spec.ts > a deployment with no identity system refuses honestly rather than showing an empty list

Tests skipped in ALL THREE once this step exists: exactly two, both media-rig rows. They are RIG rows in PW-0601's matrix, they need the commander's hardware, and they remain skipped with their reasons intact -- which the acceptance requires and which this measurement confirms rather than hopes.

THE NARROW INVOCATION WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED, WITH THE REASON. The acceptance invites naming the two spec files if that buys the same coverage for less. It was measured: the dominant cost is the production build, which either invocation pays and turbo serves from cache in this job, leaving 75 seconds of test time. Against that, naming two files would put a hand-maintained list of what matters into this workflow -- the same defect PL-0714 removed from the suite steps above it and PL-0726 removed from the migration step below it, in this very file, this round and last. A future test that became third-configuration-only would be covered by the whole-suite step and missed by the narrow one, silently, which is precisely how these three were lost for eight rounds.

THE RUN. `npm test -- --project=api --project=chromium --reporter=list,json,html` with LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=production and NO LIBERTY_E2E_DATABASE_URL. The absence is the configuration: src/env.ts derives the auth secret from that variable's presence, so a production run without it IS a deployment with no identity system. Nothing is stubbed and no test is told it is special.

`html` IS NAMED ON THE COMMAND LINE DELIBERATELY, and finding out why was a defect caught before commit: --reporter on the CLI REPLACES the config's reporter list rather than adding to it, so the first draft wrote no e2e/playwright-report at all and the upload step would have archived nothing. Verified after the fix: both /tmp/verify-reporters.json and e2e/playwright-report/index.html are produced.

THE GUARD, AND THE FIVE WAYS IT WAS PROVEN TO REFUSE. The acceptance says evidence must be "the run naming them as passed, not a count that went up", so a step reads the JSON report and requires all three BY NAME, each present and each "expected". It was extracted from the workflow with yaml.safe_load -- so what was executed is the text CI will execute -- and driven against real reports:

  A. the real third-configuration report      -> exit 0, three "ran and passed" notices naming each title and its project
  B. the real production+PostgreSQL report    -> exit 1, three errors, each saying the title is "skipped", not "expected"
  C. the real development report              -> exit 1, three errors
  D. a report with one title renamed          -> exit 1, "No test matching ... is in the report at all. It was renamed or deleted"
  E. no report file at all                    -> exit 1, "whether these three ran is unknown -- which is not the same as them having run"

B and C are the important ones: the guard is driven against the two configurations CI ACTUALLY RUNS TODAY and goes red on both. It would have caught the original defect. A sixth case arrived unplanned while verifying the reporters -- a run of only playback-session.api.spec.ts -- and it refused on the missing watchlist title.

The step also emits the suite counts as an annotation, because annotations are the only CI channel this session can read.

NOTHING WAS WEAKENED. No test was changed, no assertion relaxed, no skip removed, no retry added, no timeout raised. The two existing suite steps are untouched -- `git diff` over this file is confined to the inserted block -- so no existing configuration loses coverage.

assigned.title: The automated half of the Windows matrix, running on Windows
assigned.acceptance: Every row PW-0601 marks automated runs on a windows-latest runner and fails the build when it fails. REQUIRED: the existing e2e suite runs against the DESKTOP target on Windows, not only the web target on Ubuntu -- the desktop axis is currently built on Ubuntu only, and only incidentally, because the axis defaults on and openssl happens to be installed. REQUIRED: the shell is driven end to end where the harness can reach it, and where it cannot, the row stays in the commander-machine half rather than being replaced by a unit test that proves something easier. REQUIRED: retries stay at zero, on the rule playwright.config.ts already states at length. REQUIRED: a row that is skipped says why, by name, the way the existing harness already does for the desktop and media-rig axes.
assigned.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict. SURFACE NOTE: this task's allowedPaths name directories that do not exist yet. The evidence-based narrowing procedure applies to reconciling work already in history; for genuinely new work the surface is the smallest set of paths the acceptance can be satisfied within, and it is narrowed again from the diff before review if it turns out to be wider than what was written. OWNERSHIP RESOLVED BY RESPONSIBILITY in round 87, on gpt-architect's ruling. .github/workflows/windows.yml moved from allowedPaths to reviewDependencies: this task is the certification CONSUMER -- it needs the workflow and the artifact to EXIST and to execute its rows, which is a read relationship. PW-0501 owns the workflow because PW-0501 produces the Windows artifact. A task does not co-own a production build workflow merely because its tests run there. If this task's acceptance genuinely requires editing that workflow after PW-0501 lands, it is sequenced AFTER PW-0501 -- its dependencies already say so -- and its narrowed write surface is derived from the actual change at claim time rather than reserved now. Neither task was narrowed to defeat conflictWithActive; the surfaces follow the implementation responsibility. ROUND 107 AMENDMENT, on gpt-architect's ruling: .github/workflows/windows.yml has MOVED from reviewDependencies to allowedPaths -- allowedPaths is always part of the reviewed surface, so leaving it in both is redundant and ai:validate says so. This is the condition the round-87 note above named -- PW-0501 has landed, and the acceptance clause 'runs on a windows-latest runner and fails the build when it fails' cannot be satisfied without writing the only file that defines one. The surface was derived at claim time from the actual change, as that note required, and is the single file rather than .github/workflows/**. scripts/windows/** was deliberately NOT taken; it remains PW-0502's and PW-0503's. Conflict check and the cost to those two tasks' future fingerprints are recorded in the task.definition_changed event of this round.

typecheck.evidence:
The workflow is machine-checked by the method rounds 107-110 established. Every `run:` block with `shell: pwsh` is extracted from the YAML by a parser -- 8 blocks across both jobs, 1 new -- with ${{ runner.temp }} and every ${{ steps.<id>.outcome }} substituted as GitHub would substitute them, and each parse-checked with [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile under PowerShell 7.4.6: 0 files with parse errors. The YAML round-trips through a parser and reports jobs [package, e2e-desktop] with all fourteen package steps now carrying an id -- previously two did. npm run repo:validate passes.

THE NEW DIAGNOSTICS STEP WAS EXECUTED ON BOTH ITS BRANCHES rather than read. With every outcome "success" it emits the warning branch: "The job failed but no step reports a non-success outcome, so the failure is in the runner or in something this list does not name", followed by the full trail. With tauri-bundle set to failure and the two steps after it left empty, it emits "FIRST FAILING STEP: tauri-bundle (failure). Everything after it did not run." and the trail renders those two as not-reached -- which is exactly the sentence Windows #14 could not produce.

e2e.evidence:
WINDOWS PACKAGE #15 (run 37210126408) AT EXACT HEAD 659cafa118bdc72b98d43c7f3fa21a120222e57b. This re-records the e2e gate with the REAL WINDOWS EXECUTION gpt-architect's round-111 verdict asked for, replacing nothing and adding what Windows #14 could not say.

THE JOB PAGE, NOT THE RUN PAGE, as round 110 established is the only trustworthy surface. Job 111459438814, e2e-desktop: CONCLUSION SUCCEEDED, 3m 25s.

ITS TWO ANNOTATIONS, VERBATIM:
  "openssl=C:\Program Files\OpenSSL\bin\openssl.exe; mode=development; database=none (GitHub service containers are Linux-only, so the production-with-identity rung stays on Ubuntu)"
  "expected=122 unexpected=0 flaky=0 skipped=29 duration=125.9s"

CLAUSE BY CLAUSE.

1. "the existing e2e suite runs against the DESKTOP target on Windows, not only the web target on Ubuntu" -- PROVEN BY A RUN. 122 cases executed and passed on a windows-latest runner against the desktop target. Not a count that went up: the job is green and the non-vacuity guard is a FAILING STEP, so green is load-bearing.

2. THE NON-VACUITY GUARD PASSED, and that is what the success actually buys. `assert-desktop-axis-ran.mjs` runs as its own step with `if: !cancelled()`, so an all-skipped axis could not have produced a green job -- the guard would have failed it. Its OWN unit tests also ran, as a separate earlier step, so a defect in the guard would have been loud rather than silent. Both are steps in a job that succeeded, which means both passed; this is inferred from the job's conclusion rather than from a log, and the inference is sound only because each is a failing step, which is why they were written that way.

3. "retries stay at zero" -- flaky=0. Playwright reports a case as flaky when it failed and then passed on a retry, so zero flaky over 151 cases means no case was retried into passing. `playwright.config.ts` sets retries: 0 and nothing overrode it.

4. "a row that is skipped says why, by name" -- 29 skipped, and here the evidence is CORROBORATION RATHER THAN DIRECT OBSERVATION, which is stated rather than glossed. The annotation gives a count; the per-row reasons are in the artifact (playwright-report-windows-desktop, 17.2 KB, sha256:dffe26c69d3eef4295d4c0d29dde9731c83cc34f662eae839dc45660dda66308), and downloading an artifact requires a login this session does not have. What CAN be said: the Windows axis runs mode=development with database=none, and the identical configuration run locally produces EXACTLY THE SAME NUMBERS -- 122 executed, 29 skipped -- with every one of the 29 carrying a stated reason and ZERO carrying none:

     22  "LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=development, where identity comes from the development headers rather than from a session store..."
      2  "Only a production-mode run with no LIBERTY_E2E_DATABASE_URL is this configuration..."
      2  "No media rig configured. Set LIBERTY_E2E_MEDIA_ORIGIN to a DASH/HLS origin you hold rights to serve from..."
      1  "This server runs a development build, where the scaffold is reachable on purpose."
      1  "this case is the refused-build half of the matrix"
      1  "This run can identify a caller, so it does not render the unconfigured-deployment branch."

   Two configurations on two platforms agreeing to the case on both numbers is strong evidence the skip sets are the same set, and it is not the same thing as having read the Windows names. Recorded as corroboration.

5. "where it cannot [drive the shell end to end], the row stays in the commander-machine half rather than being replaced by a unit test that proves something easier" -- the two media-rig rows are skipped with the reason above and remain RIG rows in PW-0601's matrix. Nothing was substituted for them.

WHAT THIS EVIDENCE DOES NOT COVER, SO IT CANNOT BE READ AS COVERING IT. The `package` job of the same run was still in progress when this was recorded, so nothing here speaks to packaging, the MSI, the lifecycle harness or F1/F2/F3/F4. Those belong to PW-0501/PW-0503/PW-0502 rather than to this task's acceptance, which is about the e2e matrix, but the distinction is stated because the round-111 directive asks about both and only one is answered here.

WHAT CHANGED SINCE WINDOWS #14. #14's e2e-desktop also succeeded, and that was already evidence for clause 1. What #14 could not give was the counts: the annotation publisher produced them for the first time here, so retries-at-zero and executed-case-count move from "the guard would have caught it" to measured values.

review.evidence:
CHANGES REQUESTED at 4a13f4593ee00aff71acb470d065c7cffa39b1a4, under gpt-architect's own round-110 condition, transcribed by claude-test. The reviewer wrote: "Do NOT approve PW-0602 from parser-only evidence if Windows #14 has not proven the new job", and required that for lifecycle "every observable row" be verified as PASS, FAIL, NOT-RUN with an exact reason, then classified as (A) workflow/harness defect, (B) product defect, (C) commander-only row or (D) genuinely unsupported CI row.

WHAT WINDOWS #14 (run 37172243171, head 4a13f45) PROVED, AND IT IS THE HALF THIS TASK WAS WRITTEN FOR. The e2e-desktop job CONCLUDED SUCCESS in 3m 35s. Its annotations read "openssl=C:\Program Files\OpenSSL\bin\openssl.exe; mode=development; database=none" and "expected=118 unexpected=0 flaky=0 skipped=24 duration=134.8s". Success is the load-bearing fact: the job contains the non-vacuity guard as a FAILING step, so a run in which the desktop axis had skipped could not have concluded success. The desktop axis therefore genuinely executed on a Windows runner, on the first attempt, with retries still at zero and the same two projects CI runs. PW-0602's first REQUIRED clause is met.

WHY THIS CANNOT BE APPROVED ANYWAY. The package job CONCLUDED FAILURE with "Process completed with exit code 1", and the only other annotation is the lifecycle publisher's own notice: "NO REPORT WAS PRODUCED. The harness writes nothing when it refuses (wrong platform, missing or bad --msi), which is a fault in this workflow rather than in the product."

THAT NOTICE CANNOT SUPPORT THE CLASSIFICATION THE REVIEWER ASKED FOR, and that is the finding. The publisher runs on `!cancelled()`, so it emits that sentence whenever no report file exists -- which is equally true if the Tauri build failed, if the inventory step threw "no msi in the inventory", if the install-verifier negative check failed, or if the harness itself refused. Only two of the package job's fourteen steps carry an `id`, so nothing on the run page names the step that exited 1. A reader is therefore invited to conclude "the harness refused over a bad --msi" when the evidence does not establish it. That is the same defect this session has now corrected three times in its own instruments: a diagnostic confidently naming a cause it has not measured.

This is category A -- a workflow/harness defect -- but it is specifically a defect in the workflow's ABILITY TO BE DIAGNOSED, and it must be fixed before any row is classified, because classifying from this annotation would be guessing. Windows #13 at 4f23c1d recorded F1 PASS, F3 PASS, F4 PASS and F2 not-run, so the package job REGRESSED between 4f23c1d and 4a13f45 and the cause is not yet known.

REQUIRED BEFORE RE-REVIEW: every step in the package job carries an id; a failure-diagnostics step names the first failing step and its outcome on the run page, in the annotation channel, as ci.yml's own failure-diagnostics already does; and the "NO REPORT" message stops asserting a cause it cannot know.

recommended.title: Install, upgrade, uninstall, reinstall — tested, not assumed
recommended.acceptance: The installer's lifecycle is exercised automatically wherever that is possible on a runner, and everything that is not is named for the commander's machine. REQUIRED: clean install on a machine that has never had the application, then launch. REQUIRED: upgrade over a previous version with user data preserved, which is the one a release breaks most often and nobody tests. REQUIRED: uninstall leaves no service, no scheduled task and no orphaned node.exe, and states exactly what user data it keeps or removes. REQUIRED: reinstall after uninstall. REQUIRED: each case is marked automated or commander-machine, with the reason, so the split is visible rather than implied.
recommended.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict. SURFACE NOTE: this task's allowedPaths name directories that do not exist yet. The evidence-based narrowing procedure applies to reconciling work already in history; for genuinely new work the surface is the smallest set of paths the acceptance can be satisfied within, and it is narrowed again from the diff before review if it turns out to be wider than what was written.

review.evidence: CHANGES REQUESTED at 835823561c69f5bbdebf19c637eeeabff19dacf7. Transcribed by claude-lead from gpt-architect's round-105 ruling, section 2, which is a request for changes in substance even though it does not use the word: 'The lifecycle harness architecture is accepted. DO NOT mark PW-0503 DONE merely to free the Test lane. Current Windows evidence establishes only part of the lifecycle matrix.' gpt's itemised verdict: F1 clean install PARTIAL PASS -- the MSI builds, installs and its installed tree is verified; still unverified is actual installed application launch and WebView runtime. F2 upgrade UNVERIFIED -- no real previous release has been exercised as an upgrade source, so user-data preservation across an actual upgrade remains unproven. F3 uninstall PARTIAL PASS -- msiexec uninstall executes; still to prove where automation permits are no orphaned service, no scheduled task, no orphaned node.exe, expected files removed, and documented user-data retention behaviour. F4 reinstall UNVERIFIED but AUTOMATABLE -- 'implement and execute this rather than classifying it as commander-only'. WHAT HAS CHANGED SINCE THAT VERDICT WAS WRITTEN, and it narrows the request rather than answering it: the IMPLEMENTATION of F3's residue classification and of F4 reinstall already exists in scripts/windows/lifecycle.mjs and residue.mjs at the commit above, with 30 cases behind the decisions, and F4 is already marked plannedAutomated with no manual portion. What does not exist is EXECUTION, and it cannot be created by any open task: no open task can write .github/workflows/windows.yml -- every writer is DONE and PW-0502, PW-0503 and PW-0602 hold it read-only. That is recorded as a board.sequencing_finding and needs a ruling on which task gets the write surface. Recorded so the task leaves REVIEW honestly rather than being completed on evidence gpt declined to accept.

recommended.title: The desktop notices suite is run by nothing, which is the fifth instance
recommended.acceptance:
apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs is 22 cases covering the licence-evidence verdicts, the rendered document, and -- added in round 111 -- the five refusals that stop the notices generator reporting success over a tree it found nothing in. NOTHING RUNS IT. apps/desktop has no package.json, so it is not an npm workspace and turbo never reaches it, and `npm run test:scripts` does not name it.

THIS IS THE FIFTH INSTANCE OF ONE DEFECT. scripts/test-validate-repo.mjs ran nowhere until PL-AI-0002; scripts/test-desktop-target.mjs and the 30-case Windows lifecycle suite ran nowhere until PL-0714; apps/web/src/components/player/tracks.ts was imported by nothing until PW-0306; three e2e titles were skipped in every configuration until PL-0717. Each time the thing existed, passed, and no gate asked it.

REQUIRED: the suite runs where a gate asks it, which means `npm run test:scripts` and therefore package.json.
REQUIRED: it runs in CI. PL-0714 made the validate job mirror test:scripts BY A MECHANISM rather than by a hand-kept list; if that mechanism picks this up automatically, say so and prove it, and if it does not, that is a defect in the mechanism and belongs in this task's finding rather than being worked around with another hand-added step.
REQUIRED: evidence that it actually executed in CI, naming the case count -- not that a step was added.

OUT OF SCOPE: changing what the suite asserts.
recommended.notes: FILED ROUND 111 by claude-infra during PW-0208. package.json is outside PW-0208's surface. PL-0728 proposes the standing mechanical check that would have caught this and the four before it; this is the individual repair and that is the general one.
